# Accessibility Evaluation Report: RiverCity Metro Member-Facing Surfaces

## Evaluation Identity
Evaluator: Meridian Digital Accessibility (reporting lead) | Commissioner: RiverCity Metro Authority, Office of Civil Rights | Dates: 2026-06-22 → 2026-07-24  
Methodology: WCAG-EM 2.0 (https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-em-2/)  
Report Version: RCM-2026Q3 Final | Evaluation ID: rcm-2026q3

## Scope
All member-facing content on rivercitymetro.org (trip planner, schedules, fares, service alerts, pass-holder account), the RideRC native app's ticket-activation flow, and monthly PDF timetables.  
**Named Exclusion:** Third-party real-time vehicle map iframe (vendor-supplied, documented as non-remediable this cycle).

## Conformance Target
WCAG 2.2 Level AA

## Accessibility Support Baseline
NVDA 2026.1 + Firefox 141 (Windows 11); VoiceOver + Safari 18 (macOS 15); TalkBack 15 + Chrome (Android 15); keyboard-only without screen reader.

## Additional Requirements
- Findings filable per bug-reporting template
- Plain-language summary for transit board

## Technologies Relied Upon
- Web: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React), WAI-ARIA
- Native app: Kotlin/Swift (not web-based)
- PDF: Untagged timetables sampled (see Coverage Boundary)

## Sample Set
**Structured (12):**  
S01–S11 (10 core templates + 2 expanded from representativeness check)  
**Random (1):** R01 = /riders/lost-and-found (10% of structured set, seed 7391)  
**Complete Processes (2):**  
P01 (web): Trip plan → buy pass (6 steps + error branch)  
P02 (native app): Ticket activation (default sequence)  
**State Coverage:** Default, loading, error, expanded states (per template capabilities). Representativeness check confirmed no further new content types after S11 addition.

## Outcomes
| WCAG SC | Outcome | Coverage | Notes |
|--------|---------|----------|-------|
| 1.1.1 | **Passed** | 100% | All images have alt text |
| 1.2.x | **Untested** | 0% | No audio/video content |
| 1.3.1 | **Failed** | 100% | PDF timetables untagged |
| 1.4.3 | **Failed** | 83% | 2.8:1 & 3.9:1 contrast violations |
| 2.1.1 | **Failed** | 100% | Fare-zone slider keyboard-inoperable |
| 2.4.1 | **Failed** | 83% | Legacy skip-link anchor missing |
| 2.4.3 | **Passed** | 100% | Focus order follows visual order |
| 2.4.7 | **Passed** | 100% | Focus indicators sufficient |
| 3.1.1 | **Passed** | 100% | All pages declare valid lang |
| 3.1.2 | **Untested** | 0% | No multilingual content |
| 3.3.1 | **Failed** | 100% | Error message not associated |
| 4.1.2 | **Failed** | 100% | Icon-only buttons missing names |
| 4.1.3 | **Failed** | 100% | Success message silent |

**Representativeness Check:**  
Random sample surfaced legacy template class (2019 "info-page") missing from structured set. Expanded structured samples with S11 to address. Second comparison found no new content types.

## Findings
- a11y_fare_zone_slider_keyboard (CRITICAL)  
- a11y_swap_button_name (MINOR)  
- a11y_route_badge_contrast (MAJOR)  
- a11y_payment_error_association (MAJOR)  
- a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor (MINOR)  
- a11y_purchase_confirm_silent (MAJOR)  
- a11y_ticket_activate_unlabeled (MAJOR)  
- a11y_timetable_pdf_untagged (MAJOR)

## Coverage Boundary
- **Web:** All samples measurable via Playwright/axe-core  
- **Native app (P02):** Manual TalkBack/VO testing required (non-web tech)  
- **PDFs:** Untagged timetables evaluated manually (no automated tooling used)  
- **Named Exclusion:** Third-party map iframe (vendor responsibility)

## Evaluation Statement
This evaluation does **not** support a WCAG 2.2 AA conformance claim for the full product due to multiple unmet success criteria (1.3.1, 1.4.3, 2.1.1, 3.3.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3). The evaluation followed WCAG-EM 2.0 methodology with sampling-based analysis. See findings for details.

## Aggregated Score
Not provided per WCAG-EM guidance: scores may mislead. Outcomes are documented per EARL vocabulary.

## Machine Readable
EARL export available at [https://example.com/earl/rcm-2026q3.xml](https://example.com/earl/rcm-2026q3.xml)

---

### Plain-Language Summary for Transit Board
The RiverCity Metro portal and app have made significant progress toward accessibility, but several critical issues remain. Key findings include:
- **Payment flow issues:** Keyboard users cannot complete purchases, and error messages are not announced.
- **Missing labels:** Important buttons (e.g., ticket activation) lack screen reader labels.
- **Contrast problems:** Some text is too light for users with visual impairments.
- **PDF accessibility:** Monthly timetables are not navigable by screen readers.

All issues are documented with severity ratings and remediation guidance. The evaluation team recommends prioritizing CRITICAL and MAJOR findings for the next remediation cycle.
